Implementing a thorough maintenance program is the most effective way to retain generator reliability
and avoid major failure expenses. However, it must be cost effective in that there are demonstrated
savings in improved availability & reliability to offset the cost of implementing the program. The three
important elements of a thorough program are maintenance frequency, electrical testing and visual
inspection.
 
Generator electrical testing is focused on the integrity of insulation systems. Changes between outage
test results may point to needed repairs/rework that may not be evident from the absolute test values
themselves.
 
A visual inspection performed by an experienced individual can disclose unit conditions not detected
by monitoring equipment or indicated by tests. In some instances electrical testing will only detect
issues when the stator and field insulation systems have significantly deteriorated. Also, for example,
there is no definitive test for contamination, rust or oil, and water leaks; yet the presence of any of
these could significantly adversely affect reliability and operation.
 
This report documents the Visual Inspection, Electrical Tests, and End Winding repairs performed on
unit#10B, Gas Turbine-Generator (337X351), of the GA Power Company at the McIntosh Generating
Station.
Following the guidelines outlined in GEK103566, the inspections were performed from March 3rd to
the 10th, 2012.
 
As recommended for Major outages, the generator field (Rotor) was removed from the stator to
perform a wide range of tests and inspections recommended during this type of outage. 
The winding neutrals and line side were disconnected and completely isolated from the outside bus at
the closest point to the generator to facilitate individual tests on each phase of the stator windings.
 
A detailed description of the tests, inspections, and recommendations are included in the body of this
report. Similarly, all relevant data sheets are attached to their appropriate sections of the report. The
inspection photos, Wedge Tightness map, and reference drawing showing locations of Axial Support
hardware, blockings, and ties on End Winding are included in the appendix
 
WORK SCOPE SUMMARY:
1.Electrical tests on Generator Stator
2.Visual Inspection on generator Stator assembly
3.Wedge tightness test on stator wedges
4.Perform TIL 1398-2R on stator Axial Support Hardware
5.Replace Loose/dusting Blockings and Ties on End Winding
6.Clean End Windings from Greasing, Dusting & Oil
7.Flood Stator End Windings with Polyester Resin
8.Paint Stator Core and End Winding (CE) after Repairs
9.Perform Visual Inspection and Clearance Check on Stator Core Belly Bands
10.Clean the High Voltage Bushings
11.Electrical tests on Generator Field
